summary:
Bangladesh has signed leases with PRAN-RFL Group and a second private group to restart three BJMC jute mills in Sirajganj and Khulna. 
The projects carry Tk 6.19 billion in planned investment and at least 11,629 jobs, signalling potential fresh capacity for jute supply chains. 
The wider programme targets reopening 20 of 25 closed BJMC mills; 14 leases are complete and nine mills have resumed.

title: Ralph Lauren crushes Q1 2026: Stock jumps 7% on strong sales
summary:
Ralph Lauren's first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue reached $1.96 billion, with adjusted earnings of $4.59 a share and constant-currency revenue up 13 per cent.
Asia led growth at 25 per cent, with China up more than 40 per cent; North America rose 13 per cent and Europe gained 5 per cent.
Full-year revenue outlook is now 5–6 per cent, with tariffs and soft Europe sentiment flagged.

title: Polyester feedstock shock could push costs higher into late August
summary:
MEG led Asia's polyester chain, with CFR SE Asia up 5.97 per cent to USD 710/mt and CFR China up 3.23 per cent to USD 640/mt.
PX and PTA export benchmarks firmed 0.5–0.9 per cent, while domestic China PTA fell 1.08 per cent to CNY 5,945.
Brent's 4.99 per cent Monday spike to USD 87.72 restored the geopolitical premium; rising feedstock costs now meet weak downstream demand.

title: Bangladesh PMI rises sharply as manufacturing hits series high in July
summary:
Bangladesh's composite PMI rose 4.9 points to 57.8 in July, moving further above the 50-point expansion mark. 
Manufacturing jumped 16.6 points to 65.4, with gains across orders, exports, output, employment, imports and deliveries. 
For garment and textile supply chains, stronger exports and improved expectations signal firmer near-term factory activity.

title: VSF's stable prices set the stage for a mid-August price breakout
summary:
VSF markets in India, China and Pakistan closed August 3–10 in near-perfect stability, with TexPro benchmarks flat in India and China.
India's 1.4D and 1.5D×38mm VSF held at ₹196/kg and ₹193/kg, while China's 1.5D×38mm stayed at CNY 14.25/kg.
Pakistan's 1.5D grade eased from PKR 639/kg to PKR 638/kg, a 0.16 per cent move linked to rupee rounding rather than fundamental pressure.

title: Vietnam targets 1500 containers/year in rail freight service to China
summary:
The rail freight route linking China’s Hebei province with Vietnam has delivered encouraging results after more than a year of operation, with improved supply chain efficiency, reduced logistics costs and transit times, and more opportunities for businesses, according to Vietnam Railway Transport. 
The firm is working with partners to further develop the service, targeting around 1,500 containers annually.

title: Does July’s rise signal improving US small business confidence?
summary:
US Small Business Optimism Index rose 2.4 points in July to 99.8, moving above its 52-year average and reaching the highest level since August 2025.
Hiring plans and job openings strengthened, signalling tighter labour conditions for suppliers and retail-linked firms.
Capital spending plans improved, while sales expectations and inventory views softened.

title: US containerised import volumes down 4.3% YoY in July 2026: Descartes
summary:
US containerised imports increased by 4.5 per cent month on month (MoM) in July, reaching around 2.5 million TEUs. 
Volumes were 4.3 per cent down YoY in the month. 
The July 2025 figure narrowly missed the overall record set in May 2022, according to Descartes Systems Group. 
In the first seven months this year, such imports were down by 0.9 per cent YoY while remaining well above pre-pandemic levels.

title: India’s cotton pressing revised upward to 339 lakh bales: CAI
summary:
Cotton Association of India has raised current-season cotton pressing to 339 lakh bales, 11 per cent above its initial estimate of 305 lakh bales.
The latest estimate is 8.5 per cent higher than 2024–25, with increases in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
Imports are projected at 62 lakh bales and closing stocks at 93.59 lakh bales by September 30, 2026.

title: Australia keeps cash rate at 4.35% as inflation stays high
summary:
Australia’s central bank kept the cash rate unchanged at 4.35 per cent in August after three increases this year, as inflation remained elevated. 
The RBA expects earlier rate hikes to slow spending, economic growth and employment, while unemployment rises gradually. 
Inflation, driven by domestic price pressures, is expected to return to the target midpoint only by early 2028.

title: China’s JASAN Group to build integrated industrial complex in Egypt
summary:
Construction of a new industrial project by China’s Zhejiang Jiansheng Group Co. Ltd, commercially known as JASAN Group, began in Egypt’s Qantara West Industrial Zone recently. 
To be implemented in three phases, the project will comprise an integrated industrial complex covering spinning and weaving, readymade and sportswear manufacturing, seamless garments, socks, accessories, elastic fabrics and dyeing.

title: RMG exports from Bangladesh declines 1.92% in July
summary:

Home textiles rose 14.37 per cent to $77.86 million, but cotton and cotton products fell 14.42 per cent to $39.71 million.

summary:

summary:

The decision is expected to boost the garment industry’s competitiveness. 
It comes at a time when labour standards, transparency and sustainability increasingly influence sourcing and investment decisions of buyers, the Jordan Chamber of Industry said.

summary:

Chinese and Turkish manufacturers are opening facilities in Egypt, drawn by labour costs and preferential trade access.
